description: Pollo en Mole is a quintessential Mexican dish, featuring tender chicken bathed in a rich, complex, and deeply flavorful sauce. This traditional mole offers a harmonious blend of chiles, spices, nuts, and a hint of chocolate, creating an unforgettable culinary experience. It is a true celebration of Mexican flavors, perfect for any special occasion or a comforting family meal.

instructions.title: Prepare Chiles and Chicken
instructions.text: First, rehydrate the dried chiles. Remove stems and seeds, then toast them lightly in a dry skillet for 30 seconds per side until fragrant. Place them in a bowl, cover with hot water, and let them soak for 20 minutes until softened. Meanwhile, season the chicken pieces generously with salt and set aside.

instructions.title: Toast Spices, Nuts, and Aromatics
instructions.text: In a dry skillet over medium heat, toast the almonds, pumpkin seeds, and sesame seeds separately until fragrant and lightly browned. Remove and set aside. In the same skillet, add a little oil and lightly fry the chopped onion and garlic until softened. Then add the cinnamon, cloves, anise seed, and peppercorns, toasting for another minute until aromatic. Add the torn tortilla and bread, frying until golden.

instructions.title: Blend the Mole Paste
instructions.text: Drain the rehydrated chiles, reserving some of the soaking liquid. Combine the softened chiles, toasted nuts and seeds, fried onion and garlic mixture, fried tortilla and bread, and the roasted tomato in a blender. Add 1 cup of hot chicken broth and blend until a very smooth paste forms. If needed, add more chile soaking liquid or chicken broth, a little at a time, to achieve a thick, pourable consistency.

instructions.title: Cook the Mole Sauce
instructions.text: Heat 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil or lard in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Carefully pour the blended mole paste into the hot oil. Stir constantly for about 15-20 minutes until the mole darkens in color and thickens considerably, resembling a rich paste. This step is crucial for developing the deep flavors of the mole.

instructions.title: Add Chicken and Simmer
instructions.text: Once the mole paste has thickened, gradually stir in the remaining hot chicken broth, a little at a time, until the sauce reaches your desired consistency. It should be thick enough to coat the back of a spoon. Add the chopped Mexican chocolate and stir until it completely melts into the sauce. Carefully add the seasoned chicken pieces to the mole sauce, ensuring they are fully submerged.

instructions.title: Finish and Serve
instructions.text: Reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let the chicken simmer gently in the mole sauce for at least 20-25 minutes, or until the chicken is tender and cooked through. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt as needed. Serve hot with warm corn tortillas, Mexican rice, and a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds for garnish.

tips: For an even richer flavor, lightly fry the dried chiles in a little oil before soaking them. This deepens their smokiness and helps release their oils.

If you cannot find all three types of chiles (ancho, pasilla, mulato), you can substitute with more ancho or pasilla, but the complexity of flavor will vary. Do not skip the Mexican chocolate; it adds a crucial depth, not sweetness.

Mole sauce can be made ahead of time and stored in the refrigerator for up to 5 days, or frozen for up to 3 months. It often tastes even better the next day as the flavors meld. Serve with warm corn tortillas and Mexican rice.
article:
Unlock the rich, complex flavors of Mexico right in your kitchen with Pollo en Mole, a dish that transcends mere sustenance to become a culinary celebration. This iconic Mexican chicken recipe, featuring succulent chicken bathed in a velvety, spice-laden mole sauce, is a testament to centuries of tradition and an art form passed down through generations. If you’ve ever wanted to delve into the heart of Mexican cuisine, mastering a classic Chicken Mole Recipe is an essential and incredibly rewarding journey.

## What is Chicken Mole?

Mole, pronounced "MOH-lay," is more than just a sauce; it's a culinary masterpiece with roots stretching back to pre-Hispanic Mexico. While there are countless varieties of mole, the most famous is Mole Poblano, originating from Puebla. This particular sauce is renowned for its incredible depth, often incorporating dozens of ingredients – a symphony of chiles, nuts, seeds, spices, fruits, and a touch of chocolate. The chocolate in mole isn't for sweetness but rather to deepen the color and round out the complex flavors, balancing the heat and earthiness of the chiles. Pollo en Mole simply refers to chicken prepared with this magnificent sauce, creating a dish that is both comforting and extraordinarily flavorful. It's a staple for special occasions, holidays, and family gatherings, symbolizing warmth, tradition, and culinary artistry. Crafting your own Chicken Mole Recipe from scratch allows you to appreciate the intricate balance that makes this dish so beloved.

## Ingredients for Authentic Pollo en Mole

Creating an authentic Chicken Mole Recipe requires a diverse array of ingredients, each playing a vital role in building the sauce's characteristic depth and complexity. Don't be intimidated by the list; the process is more about layering flavors than individual difficulty.

For the Chicken:
*   2-3 lbs bone-in, skin-on chicken pieces (thighs and drumsticks are ideal for flavor and moisture)
*   1 white onion, quartered
*   2-3 cloves garlic, smashed
*   1 bay leaf
*   Salt to taste

For the Mole Sauce:
*   **Dried Chiles:**
    *   4-5 ancho chiles (mild, fruity, smoky)
    *   3-4 mulato chiles (mild, smoky, chocolatey)
    *   2-3 pasilla chiles (mild, earthy, licorice notes)
    *   1-2 arbol chiles (for a touch of heat, optional)
*   **Aromatics & Spices:**
    *   1/2 white onion, roughly chopped
    *   2-3 cloves garlic
    *   1/4 cup sesame seeds
    *   1/4 cup slivered almonds
    *   1/4 cup pumpkin seeds (pepitas)
    *   1/4 cup raisins
    *   1/4 cup dried plantain chips or 1 small ripe plantain, sliced (optional)
    *   1 small piece Mexican cinnamon stick (about 1-2 inches)
    *   3-4 whole cloves
    *   1/2 teaspoon whole black peppercorns
    *   1/4 teaspoon anise seeds
    *   Pinch of dried oregano and thyme
*   **Thickener & Flavor Enhancers:**
    *   2-3 tablespoons lard or vegetable oil
    *   1-2 slices stale bread or a few corn tortillas, torn
    *   1-2 tomatoes, roughly chopped, or 1/2 can (4 oz) diced tomatoes
    *   2-3 tablespoons dark chocolate (Mexican chocolate is best, or good quality dark chocolate 70%+)
    *   1-2 tablespoons sugar or piloncillo (Mexican brown sugar cone), to taste
    *   4-6 cups reserved chicken broth
    *   Salt to taste

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Chicken Mole

Mastering this classic Chicken Mole Recipe involves several stages, but each step is crucial for developing the sauce's rich character.

1.  **Cook the Chicken:** Place chicken pieces in a large pot with quartered onion, smashed garlic, bay leaf, and a generous pinch of salt. Cover with water and bring to a boil. Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken is tender. Remove chicken and set aside. Strain and reserve the broth – you'll need 4-6 cups for the mole.
2.  **Prepare the Chiles:** Stem and seed all dried chiles. Heat a dry comal or skillet over medium heat and toast the chiles for 30-60 seconds per side until fragrant but not burnt (they should be pliable). Be careful not to over-toast, as they will become bitter. Transfer toasted chiles to a bowl, cover with hot water, and let them rehydrate for 20-30 minutes until soft.
3.  **Toast Nuts, Seeds & Spices:** In a clean skillet with a tablespoon of lard or oil, toast the sesame seeds, almonds, pumpkin seeds, raisins, and plantain (if using) individually until lightly golden and fragrant. Set aside. In the same pan, lightly toast the cinnamon stick, cloves, peppercorns, anise seeds, oregano, and thyme.
4.  **Sauté Aromatics & Bread:** Add a little more oil to the skillet if needed. Sauté the chopped onion and garlic until softened. Add the torn bread or tortillas and fry until golden. Add the chopped tomatoes and cook for 5-7 minutes until softened.
5.  **Blend the Sauce Base:** Drain the rehydrated chiles, reserving some of the soaking liquid. In a high-speed blender, combine the rehydrated chiles, all the toasted nuts, seeds, spices, sautéed aromatics, bread, and tomatoes. Add 1-2 cups of the reserved chicken broth. Blend until incredibly smooth, adding more broth or chile soaking liquid as needed. This may take several minutes and require stopping to scrape down the sides. For a truly silky sauce, pass the blended mixture through a fine-mesh sieve.
6.  **Simmer the Mole:** In a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven, heat 1-2 tablespoons of lard or oil over medium heat. Carefully pour in the blended mole sauce. It will splatter, so use caution. Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer, stirring frequently to prevent sticking. Cook for at least 30-45 minutes, or even up to 1-2 hours, adding chicken broth as needed to reach your desired consistency (it should be thick but pourable). The longer it simmers, the deeper the flavors will develop.
7.  **Add Chocolate and Seasoning:** After the mole has simmered and thickened, stir in the dark chocolate and sugar/piloncillo. Continue to simmer until the chocolate is fully melted and incorporated. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and more sugar if necessary. The sauce should be a balance of savory, sweet, and earthy, with a subtle warmth.
8.  **Combine Chicken and Mole:** Gently add the cooked chicken pieces to the simmering mole sauce. Spoon the sauce over the chicken and let it simmer together for another 15-20 minutes to allow the flavors to meld and the chicken to heat through.

## Pro Tips for the Best Chicken Mole

Creating an exquisite Chicken Mole Recipe is an art, and these tips will elevate your dish:

*   **Don't Rush the Chiles:** Toasting chiles properly is crucial. A dry skillet over medium heat until fragrant and slightly pliable is perfect. Burning them will result in a bitter sauce.
*   **Blend Thoroughly:** A powerful blender is your best friend. Blend the sauce until it's incredibly smooth. If you don't have a high-speed blender, strain the sauce through a fine-mesh sieve after blending to remove any fibrous bits.
*   **Low and Slow Simmer:** Mole improves with time. Simmering the sauce for at least an hour, or even two, allows the flavors to deepen and meld beautifully. Stir frequently to prevent scorching.
*   **Balance is Key:** Taste as you go. The mole should be complex, not overwhelmingly sweet or spicy. Adjust salt, sugar, and even a touch more chocolate if needed to find that perfect balance.
*   **Day-Old Deliciousness:** Like many stews and sauces, mole often tastes even better the next day as the flavors continue to develop.

## Serving Suggestions for Pollo en Mole

Pollo en Mole is a hearty and satisfying meal on its own, but it truly shines when served with traditional accompaniments. Hot corn tortillas are a must for scooping up every last drop of that incredible sauce. A side of fluffy Mexican rice (arroz rojo) and a simple garnish of toasted sesame seeds add texture and visual appeal. For a fresh contrast, a sprinkle of chopped cilantro or a side of pickled red onions can cut through the richness.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the traditional Chicken Mole Recipe is a classic, don't hesitate to experiment:

*   **Protein Alternatives:** Instead of chicken, try this mole with pork shoulder, turkey, or even firm tofu or roasted vegetables for a vegetarian option.
*   **Chile Combinations:** Feel free to adjust the chile blend based on availability or desired heat level. For more heat, add more arbol chiles or a few serranos. For less, omit the spicier ones.
*   **Nut & Seed Adjustments:** If you have allergies, substitute nuts with sunflower seeds or omit them entirely, increasing other thickeners like bread or tortillas.
*   **Speedier Mole:** While the traditional method is worth it, pre-made mole paste (available in Mexican grocery stores) can significantly reduce prep time. Simply dilute with chicken broth and simmer.

Embark on this culinary adventure and discover the magic of Pollo en Mole. This authentic Chicken Mole Recipe is more than just a meal; it's an experience that connects you to the vibrant heart of Mexican culture. Enjoy the process, savor the aromas, and delight in the unforgettable taste of this truly special dish.
